cards.q: Smooth ER vs rough ER: what is the difference?
cards.a: Rough ER has ribosomes stuck to its outer surface. Smooth ER has none.

cards.q: Why does rough ER look rough under a microscope?
cards.a: Bound ribosomes dot its outer surface.

cards.q: What kind of molecules does smooth ER help make?
cards.a: Lipids - oils, phospholipids, and steroids.

cards.q: Why are ovary and testis cells rich in smooth ER?
cards.a: They make steroid sex hormones, and smooth ER has the enzymes for steroid synthesis.

cards.q: What does smooth ER do in liver cells?
cards.a: Its enzymes detoxify drugs, alcohol, and other harmful substances.

cards.q: Why do people build up tolerance to some drugs?
cards.a: Repeated exposure makes liver cells grow more smooth ER and detox enzymes, so the drug is cleared faster.

cards.q: Why can abusing one drug make other drugs less effective?
cards.a: Detox enzymes act on related chemicals too, so extra smooth ER breaks down other drugs, like some antibiotics.

cards.q: What does smooth ER store in muscle cells?
cards.a: Calcium ions.

cards.q: What makes a muscle cell contract?
cards.a: A nerve signal makes calcium ions rush out of the smooth ER into the cytosol.

cards.q: What does rough ER make for the cell to secrete?
cards.a: Secretory proteins, made by its bound ribosomes. Example: insulin.

cards.q: What is insulin and where is it made?
cards.a: A hormone made and secreted by certain pancreas cells, then carried in the blood.

cards.q: What causes type 1 diabetes?
cards.a: The insulin-making pancreas cells are destroyed, so a lack of insulin disrupts glucose metabolism.

cards.q: What happens to a new polypeptide as it enters the rough ER?
cards.a: It is threaded into the ER cavity and folds into its 3-D shape.

cards.q: What is a glycoprotein?
cards.a: A protein with short sugar chains attached. Glyco means sugar.

cards.q: What is a transport vesicle?
cards.a: A vesicle that buds off a membrane and carries molecules from one part of the cell to another.

cards.q: Order the steps for a secretory protein in rough ER.
cards.a: Made by bound ribosome, enters ER and folds, sugars added, packed in a transport vesicle that buds off.

cards.q: Where does the vesicle from the rough ER go next?
cards.a: To the Golgi apparatus for more processing, then to the plasma membrane for release.

cards.q: How is rough ER a membrane factory?
cards.a: It adds membrane proteins and phospholipids to its own membrane, then ships pieces off in vesicles.

cards.q: Where do the protein-making instructions in mRNA come from?
cards.a: From a gene in the DNA in the nucleus.

cards.q: Why is the ER called a biosynthetic workshop?
cards.a: It makes many molecules: phospholipids for membranes, steroid hormones, and proteins for secretion.
